draft.title: Financial risk
card: Financial risk is the chance that you lose money or cannot meet payments. It can come from a single event, such as losing your job, or from the whole economy, such as a recession.
the value of shares or property can fall as well as rise. You may get back less than you put in.
you must repay a loan even if your income drops. A larger loan or a higher interest rate means a higher repayment and more risk.

Spreading money across different investments is called diversifying. If one falls, the others may hold their value, so the loss is smaller. Example: $10 000 in one company could lose $4000 if it falls 40%. Spread over five companies, the same fall in one costs $800.
draft.remember: Risk is the chance of losing money. Spreading it across many investments reduces the damage from any one.

a.q: Sam puts $6000 into the shares of one company. Its price falls by 30%. How much does Sam lose?
a.why: 30% of $6000 = 0.3 × $6000 = $1800. $4200 is what the shares are worth after the fall, not the loss.

b.q: Priya has $10 000. She puts $2000 into each of five different companies. One company's shares fall by 50%, and the other four do not change in value. How much does she lose in total?
b.why: Only $2000 was in the company that fell. 50% of $2000 = $1000. Losing $5000 would be the result if all $10 000 had been in that one company.
b.clue: Only the money in the falling company is affected.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's diversification example is correct ($4000 against $800), and both questions have one clear right answer that matches the explanations.
